titleEn: Stab Wound to the Abdomen With Evisceration

patient.name: Marcus Reid
patient.affectEn: pale, frightened, groaning and shivering; lying on his back on the floor with his knees drawn up, both hands pressing a blood-soaked bar towel to his left lower abdomen and trying to keep it there; smells of alcohol but is clear-headed and oriented
patient.speechEn: awake and alert, speaks in full sentences, wincing; answers only what he is asked ('he stabbed me... I can see my guts')

scene.settingEn: The back hallway of a pub in Langley, just after midnight (dispatch 2355). Good lighting. The floor is wet with spilled drink and some broken glass has been swept against the wall. The patient lies on the floor with about 500 mL of blood around him. Two RCMP officers stand at the end of the hallway; the scene is secure, the weapon has been seized and the knife is in an evidence bag, its blade about 10 cm long. One patient. Hospital is 10 minutes away.
hazardsEn: wet floor (spilled drink) and broken glass swept against the wall
blood on the floor (about 500 mL) - splash exposure
RCMP on scene: scene secure, the second patient has left with the officers, the weapon is seized

bystanders.who: bar staff (led you down the hallway)
bystanders.knowsEn: The patient slid down the wall, never lost consciousness, and they laid him on the floor. They have been holding a bar towel on the wound until you came. The second patient left with the officers. They will clear the hallway, hold doors and help with the stretcher or the lift if you tell them exactly what to do.

bystanders.who: two RCMP officers (end of the hallway)
bystanders.knowsEn: The scene is secure and the weapon has been seized: the knife is in an evidence bag, its blade about 10 cm long. He was stabbed once during a fight. The second patient has left with the officers. They know nothing about his medical history. They will clear the hallway or hold doors if asked.

scene.partnerEn: one partner at your licence level; acts only on your delegation
equipmentEn: oxygen kit with non-rebreather mask and nasal cannula
moist sterile dressings with sterile saline, dry sterile dressings and an occlusive dressing
trauma dressings, roller bandages and tape
stretcher (cot) with a scoop stretcher or slide sheet
Entonox kit, oral acetaminophen and oral ibuprofen
PCP only: IV start kit and tubing with normal saline

dispatchEn: 2355 hrs. Code 3 to a pub in Langley. A fight has left a 28-year-old male stabbed in the abdomen; a second patient has minor injuries. RCMP are on scene. Hospital is 10 minutes away.
dispatchUpdateEn: Dispatch update en route: RCMP report the scene is secure. The second patient has left with the officers and the weapon has been seized. Bar staff are holding a towel on the wound.
arrivalEn: 0004 hrs. Bar staff lead you down the back hallway of the pub. The lighting is good; the floor is wet with spilled drink and some broken glass has been swept against the wall. Two RCMP officers stand at the end of the hallway; the knife is in an evidence bag, its blade about 10 cm long. The scene is secure. Your partner is right behind you with the kits. One patient.
firstLookEn: A pale man lying on his back on the floor with his knees drawn up, awake and watching you, groaning and shivering. Both hands press a blood-soaked bar towel to his left lower abdomen. About 500 mL of blood is on the floor around him.

primary.locEn: Awake and alert (AVPU = A): speaks in full sentences ('he stabbed me... I can see my guts'). He smells of alcohol but is clear-headed and oriented.
primary.airwayEn: Clear. He is speaking in full sentences.
primary.breathingEn: Rate 24, shallow. No chest wounds, air entry equal.
primary.circulationEn: Right radial pulse 124, weak, regular. The towel is soaked and dark blood is oozing from the abdominal wound; no other bleeding.
primary.rbsEn: When the abdomen is exposed: ONE 4 cm horizontal wound left of the umbilicus with a loop of small bowel about 10 cm long protruding, pink and glistening, dark blood oozing from the wound edge; abdomen guarded. No other wounds on the chest, flanks, groin, arms or legs; the back is seen only if he is moved. Skin pale, cool, clammy (skin is given automatically during the RBS). If a dry dressing is applied it sticks to the bowel; if the bowel is pushed back in he screams and the bleeding restarts. C-spine not indicated: a single penetrating wound to the abdomen, not struck on the head or neck, no neck pain.

history.ccEn: I got stabbed in the stomach.

opqrst.oEn: I was standing at the bar. A guy I didn't know pulled a folding knife and stabbed me once. It was about 2348, I think. Then I slid down the wall and the staff laid me on the floor.
opqrst.pEn: It's worse when I move and when I cough.
opqrst.qEn: Sharp. Burning. It doesn't let up.
opqrst.rEn: It doesn't go anywhere. It's just at the wound.
opqrst.tEn: It was about 2348, about sixteen minutes before you got here. It hasn't let up since.

history.painScoreEn: Eight out of ten at first. Once the second set of vitals is unlocked (about 6 minutes later) he says seven out of ten.

sample.sEn: My guts are out. I'm lightheaded, cold and thirsty. I haven't thrown up, I have no chest pain, and I can breathe okay.
sample.mEn: Pantoprazole, 40 milligrams every day. I took two acetaminophen, 500 milligrams each, at nine tonight for a headache.
sample.pEn: I had a stomach ulcer last year. Nothing else. I weigh about 80 kilos.
sample.lEn: A burger and fries around seven, and two beers. The last beer was around ten-thirty.
sample.eEn: I was standing at the bar when a guy I didn't know pulled a folding knife and stabbed me once. The blade was about ten centimetres long and two wide - a stab, not a slash. Just the one wound, nothing else, and nobody hit me on the head or neck. I slid down the wall and I never passed out.

fe.cnsEn: I'm lightheaded when I lift my head. No headache.
fe.respiratoryEn: No shortness of breath. It hurts at the wound when I take a deep breath.
fe.cardiovascularEn: My heart is pounding. No chest pain.
fe.giGuEn: Just the wound pain. I haven't thrown up. No blood in my stool or my urine.
fe.musculoskeletalEn: No back pain and no pain in my arms or legs.
fe.endocrineEn: No, nothing like that. I'm not diabetic.

findings.headNeckEn: No trauma. Trachea midline, neck veins flat.
findings.chestLungsEn: Clear, with equal air entry in all 6 sites. No wounds or tenderness.
findings.abdomenEn: Dressing intact over the single 4 cm wound left of the umbilicus with the bowel covered, no new bleeding through (if the bowel has not been covered it is still exposed). Abdomen guarded and tender in all quadrants, not distended. Pelvis stable. If the dressing is lifted to look, he screams and the bleeding restarts.
findings.backEn: No wounds or tenderness (seen only if he is moved).
findings.lowerExtremitiesEn: Circulation, sensation and movement intact; pulses weak but present.
findings.upperExtremitiesEn: Radial pulses weak, circulation, sensation and movement intact. IV site clean and flushing freely (PCP, if an IV has been started).

vitalsSets.unlockNoteEn: baseline, en route, before fluids or TXA (required before initiating a protocol)
vitalsSets.spo2: 96% on room air (99% on 15 L NRB)

vitalsSets.unlockNoteEn: 6 minutes after set 1, en route (PCP: after the first 500 mL of the bolus): improving or holding steady, the bleeding is still internal and transport continues. The scenario gives only the changed values; pulse rhythm and strength, breathing depth and character are carried over from set 1 (the en-route exam finds the pulses still weak)

stateChanges.examinerLineEn: The dry dressing sticks to the bowel.
He screams, and the bleeding from the wound restarts.
He screams, and the bleeding from the wound restarts.

expected.actionEn: Acknowledge; plan oxygen, moist sterile dressings with an occlusive layer, warmth, IV equipment (PCP), minimal-movement lift and early transport
Recognize from dispatch a likely unstable penetrating torso injury (a stabbing to the abdomen); note that a second patient has already left with police
Confirm with dispatch that police have secured the scene and the weapon before approaching
triggers: stage until the scene is secure
scene secure before we go in

expected.actionEn: Anticipate blood exposure: PPE incl eye protection
Verbalize hazards (broken glass, wet floor, blood; police have the scene and the weapon), environment, MOI (stabbed once in a fight), one patient; estimate blood loss
Don gloves and eye protection (blood splash risk)
First look: pale male lying on his back with knees drawn up, awake, blood-soaked towel on the left lower abdomen, blood on the floor
triggers: a lot of blood on the floor

expected.actionEn: Ask police one question about what they know (weapon, number of wounds), then go straight to the patient - no time spent on a scene debrief
triggers: how many times was he stabbed

expected.actionEn: Assess LOC / AVPU: Alert
triggers: do you know where you are

expected.actionEn: Verbalize c-spine not indicated: single penetrating wound to the abdomen, not struck on the head or neck, no neck pain (p.25)
triggers: not struck on the head or neck
no neck pain so no c-spine

expected.actionEn: Assess airway
triggers: he's talking so the airway is clear

expected.actionEn: Assess breathing: rate, depth, chest for wounds, air entry both sides
Assess circulation: radial pulse rate and strength; recognize shock; control any external hemorrhage
triggers: check the pulse on the right
rate and strength of the pulse

expected.actionEn: Rapid body survey: expose and find the single 4 cm wound and the protruding bowel, check chest, flanks, groin and limbs for other wounds, then cover the bowel with a moist sterile dressing followed by an occlusive layer - do not push it back or pack the wound (p.32, p.19)
Note skin: pale, cool, clammy
High-flow oxygen 15 L NRB (trauma and shock) to keep SpO2 94% or higher (p.11, p.54)
Leave him supine in his position of comfort with the knees drawn up; limit movement; keep him warm with blankets (p.32, p.54)
Categorize as RTC (major penetrating torso trauma, p.7; pale cool clammy skin from shock) and act with urgency
Packaged and ready to load within 15 minutes; secondary survey (history, vitals, head-to-toe) en route, not on scene
Delegate bar staff and police effectively (hallway, doors, stretcher, lift)
Move him with the least movement possible - one coordinated lift with a scoop or slide sheet, knees kept up, dressing undisturbed (limit patient movement, p.32)
triggers: keep his knees up for the lift

expected.actionEn: Establish chief complaint: stabbed in the abdomen
HxC/C using the stabbing questions (p.13): weapon and blade size, stab or slash, number of wounds, other injuries, initial position and condition, LOC, plus pain features
triggers: was it a stab or a slash

expected.actionEn: Time of injury (2348) and weight (about 80 kg) - needed for the TXA window and the bolus calculation
triggers: how long ago did this happen

expected.actionEn: Pain score (8/10)
PMHx (stomach ulcer) - a contraindication check for ibuprofen
Medications incl pantoprazole and the acetaminophen taken at 2100 (within 4 hours) - contraindication checks for the oral analgesics
Allergies (none known) - also relevant to TXA
LOI (burger and fries, two beers)
GCS with components (15: E4 V5 M6)
BP by auscultation - recognize SBP 88 (below 90) as a Hypovolemia protocol criterion
Pulse rate/strength/rhythm
Respirations rate/depth/character
Skin hands-on: temperature, colour, condition
Pupils
SpO2 with calibration
State BGL and temperature are not indicated (alert, not diabetic, cause evident)
triggers: alert and not diabetic so no BGL

expected.actionEn: FE - General health
FE - CNS
FE - Respiratory
FE - Cardiovascular
FE - GI/GU (pertinent: vomiting, blood in stool or urine)
FE - Integumentary
FE - Musculoskeletal
FE - Endocrine
FE - EENT
Head/neck exam incl neck veins and trachea
Chest exam with 6-site auscultation, bilateral comparison
Abdomen exam without disturbing the dressing: inspect, check the dressing is intact and not bleeding through, gentle palpation away from the wound; check the pelvis is stable
triggers: gentle palpation away from the wound

expected.actionEn: Back exam as far as the single controlled movement allowed
Lower extremities: CSM, pulses
Upper extremities: radial pulses, CSM, IV site (PCP)
Wound management skill: moist sterile (saline) dressing over the bowel, an occlusive layer over it, secured without pressure, bowel not pushed back, wound not packed, dressing left undisturbed

Execute the Abdominal Injuries protocol: control external hemorrhage, limit movement, protect against heat loss, moist dressing plus occlusive layer, NEVER place the bowel back, position of comfort, transport (p.32)
triggers: do not push the bowel back
never put the bowel back in

expected.actionEn: Hypovolemia protocol with the indications stated (blood loss, SBP 88 below 90, signs of shock) and baseline vitals done: supine, warm, oxygen to SpO2 94% or higher, rapid transport (p.54)
triggers: blood loss with a systolic under 90
signs of shock and a low pressure

expected.actionEn: Pain management (Appendix A): rule out each drug's contraindications aloud and name the reasons - Entonox withheld (shock, p.65), ibuprofen withheld (ulcer history / possible bowel bleeding, p.68), acetaminophen withheld (taken within the past 4 hours, p.58)
triggers: no ibuprofen because of the ulcer
no acetaminophen he took some at nine

expected.actionEn: PCP: vascular access en route with aseptic technique and a 20 mL/kg bolus (80 kg = 1,600 mL, max 2 L) reassessed every 500 mL (p.54, p.32, p.38)

PCP: TXA 2 g IV push over the full minute with the 6 rights, after stating the indication and checking the contraindications (injury 2348 - within 3 hours; no hypersensitivity; adult; no isolated TBI); record the time (p.78)
triggers: less than three hours since the injury

expected.actionEn: Reassure him and ask him to stay still and not touch the dressing; keep him warm
triggers: I'm going to take care of you

expected.actionEn: Reassess ABCs, IV site (PCP) and warmth after each major move and after every 500 mL (p.10)
Recheck the dressing is moist, in place and not bleeding through - without lifting it to look
triggers: check the dressing without lifting it

expected.actionEn: Second full vitals within 5-6 minutes; interpret the trend and the pain score (7/10)
PCP: reassess BP after each 500 mL of the bolus and continue per the reassessment while transport carries on (p.54)
If the dressing slips or dries, re-cover with a fresh moist sterile dressing and occlusive layer - never push the bowel back (p.32)
triggers: re-cover with a fresh moist dressing

expected.actionEn: En-route notification for a critical patient: stabbing, evisceration, shock, ETA
Complete hand-off: mechanism and weapon, time of injury, findings, baseline versus repeat vitals
Treatments and times: dressing, fluids, TXA time; analgesics withheld and why; PMHx, medications incl the 2100 acetaminophen, allergies, LOI
Accurate PCR within 5 minutes (time of injury, TXA time, bolus volume, pain scores)
triggers: time of injury and TXA time

specialEvents.descriptionEn: candidate covers the protruding bowel with a DRY dressing, dry gauze, a towel or a bandage only (no sterile saline moisture)
candidate actually puts an occlusive layer (occlusive dressing, plastic wrap or similar) over the moist dressing on the bowel. Saying they would do it later is NOT this event
candidate pushes, tucks or replaces the protruding bowel back into the abdomen (or tells the partner or a bystander to)
candidate packs the abdominal wound (pushes gauze or a dressing into the wound)

candidate lifts, peels back or removes the dressing over the bowel to look at the bowel or wound again after it was applied. Checking the outside of the dressing for bleed-through, adding a fresh moist dressing and occlusive layer over a dressing that slipped or dried, and removing the bar towel to expose the wound at the start are NOT this event
candidate moves him more than necessary: sits him up, stands him up or walks him, rolls him repeatedly, drags him, or lifts him roughly without a coordinated lift and with the knees straightened
PCP says they push the TXA faster than over the full 1 minute (for example 'push it over 10 seconds' or 'rapid push')
PCP runs the fluid bolus past 500 mL, or hangs the next bag, without reassessing the patient (BP / vitals / ABCs) in between

drugs.doseEn: 2 g (2000 mg) IV push over the full 1 minute - single dose; PCP only, after the Hypovolemia protocol has started and the baseline vitals are done
drugs.indicationsEn: major trauma after the Hypovolemia protocol has started; signs of shock with a penetrating abdominal injury and ongoing bleeding; injury at about 2348 so he is well inside the 3-hour window
drugs.contraindicationsEn: known hypersensitivity or allergy to TXA (none known); more than 3 hours after injury; patient under 12 years; isolated TBI
drugs.cautionsEn: further hypotension if administered too quickly

drugs.doseEn: 20 mL/kg IV bolus to a maximum of 2 L: 80 kg = 1,600 mL, reassessing every 500 mL; target systolic BP 90; en route with aseptic technique
self-administered by inhalation - WITHHELD in this scenario: shock is a listed caution (p.65). If given, report drug:entonox
oral - WITHHELD in this scenario: stomach ulcer history and possible bleeding from the injured bowel (p.68 lists active GI hemorrhage or ulcers as a contraindication). If given, report drug:ibuprofen
oral - WITHHELD in this scenario: he took two 500 mg tablets at 2100, within the past 4 hours (p.58). If given, report drug:acetaminophen

examinerPrompts.missedInjuryEn: You have dealt with the abdominal wound - what did the rest of your rapid body survey show? What about the chest, flanks, groin, arms and legs?

trackNotes.emrEn: EMR: control external bleeding, cover the bowel with a moist sterile dressing and an occlusive layer (never replace it), leave him supine in his position of comfort with the knees up, keep him warm, high-flow oxygen, limit movement, and RTC with the secondary survey en route. No IV, no fluid bolus, no TXA. Pain: Entonox, ibuprofen and acetaminophen are all withheld with the reasons stated (shock, p.65; ulcer history and possible bowel bleeding, p.68; acetaminophen within 4 hours, p.58). (Textbook practice - not a BC rubric item: nothing by mouth with an open abdomen; nitrous oxide expands gas-filled bowel.) At the second check an EMR candidate with no fluids is holding steady rather than improving (BP 90/56, pulse 120, resps 24); the sheet's set 2 values are the PCP readings.
trackNotes.pcpEn: PCP adds, en route, vascular access, a 20 mL/kg bolus (80 kg = 1,600 mL, max 2 L) reassessed every 500 mL with the SBP target of 90 from p.48, and TXA 2 g IV push over 1 minute once the Hypovolemia protocol has started (injury 2348, inside the 3-hour limit), plus the 9-system Functional Enquiry en route. (Textbook practice - not a BC rubric item: many systems accept a lower pressure target in penetrating torso trauma; the BC guideline gives the 20 mL/kg bolus and q500 mL reassessment.)

sourcePages: Scenario tr-10 (data/practical/scenarios-2.json): dispatch, scene, primary, transport, history, vitals sets 1-2, FE, exam, interventions, ongoing, handoff. BC Provincial Examination Guidelines (current to June 15, 2026): p.6 Patient Assessment Model (load and transport at the decision point); p.7 Findings in Unstable Patients (major penetrating trauma to the torso; cool pale clammy skin secondary to suspected shock); p.10 Load and transport (reassess the ABCI after each major move; notification); p.11 Primary survey interventions (oxygen for trauma and evidence of shock); p.13 Stabbing history questions (weapon, size, slashed or stabbed, number of wounds, other injuries, initial position and condition, loss of consciousness); p.19 Wound Care (expose and examine; do not pack wounds on the neck, chest or abdomen); p.25 Spinal Management (NEXUS / Canadian C-Spine indications); p.32 Abdominal Injuries (control external hemorrhage, limit movement, protect against heat loss, cover extruded bowel with moist sterile dressings followed by an occlusive layer, do not place back, position of comfort, transport; PCP en route: vascular access, correct hypoperfusion, TXA if indicated); p.38 IV Procedures (aseptic technique); p.48 fluid bolus 20 mL/kg to a maximum of 2 L, reassessing every 500 mL, target systolic BP 90; p.54 Hypovolemia (systolic BP < 90, signs of shock; supine, warm, oxygen to SpO2 >= 94%; PCP vascular access and fluid bolus); p.58 Acetaminophen (not if given within the past 4 hours); p.65 Entonox (caution: shock); p.68 Ibuprofen (contraindication: active GI hemorrhage or ulcers); p.78 Tranexamic Acid (2 g IV push over 1 minute; contraindicated if more than 3 hours after injury, under 12 years, isolated TBI; caution: further hypotension if given too quickly).
